title: The hunter who swept the ants
hookLine: a cruel hunter meets Narada, and climbs
carry: prema grows rung by rung, starting with company
tomorrow: a teacher asks a boy, who are you? his answer turns down every label.
last: A SLIGHT TOUCH CAN BEGIN IT.

cards: Chaitanya tells this story to Sanatana, Rupa's brother, in the Chaitanya Charitamrita. Narada, walking through a forest, finds deer and boars lying half-killed, left to suffer.
The hunter, Mrigari, does it on purpose; his father taught him. Narada tells him plainly: the pain you give will come back to you. The hunter is shaken, and asks what to do.
Break your bow, says Narada. But how will I eat? I'll see that you're fed.
So the hunter breaks his bow, builds a hut by the river, and sits chanting the name beside a tulasi plant, and the villagers start bringing him food. Later, Narada comes to visit.

teach.b: Rupa set down a ladder, and many teachers walk this hunter up it. In paraphrase, the rungs are: faith. The company of devotees.
The falling away of what doesn't belong. Steadiness. Taste.
Attachment. Bhava. And then prema rises.
Watch the hunter go up. Faith, the moment Narada's words land. Company, Narada himself.
The work: the name, by the river. Then the falling away, and nobody forces it. The cruelty simply goes, until even an ant matters.
Steadiness, taste, attachment: the name he began chanting because he was told to becomes the thing he wants. Rupa describes bhava, near the top, as like a ray of the sun of prema.
A ray is already sunlight; it just isn't the whole sun yet.
Then prema: bhava grown dense, the heart made completely soft, with a deep sense that Krishna is one's own. That's the teaching. In this lineage, love for God isn't a switch.

It grows rung by rung, and the rung after faith is people. Here the first division of Rupa's ocean ends. Tomorrow the track turns to a different Hindu path, the path of knowing, with a different teacher.

how: Some Gaudiya Vaishnava communities teach this ladder to newcomers and use it to describe a devotional life that starts with faith and good company. The story of the hunter is a favorite in their classes.

games.q: what does “rupa goswami's bhakti rasamrita sindhu” mean?
o: a ladder of temple duties for new priests
a list of penalties for broken vows
a book whose opening climbs from faith to prema

p: a hunter who came to sweep ants from his path
like a ray of the sun of prema
bhava grown dense, the heart made soft

s: love for God is either there or it isn't, like a switch
Rupa sets down a ladder: steadiness, taste and attachment grow before bhava and prema.
on Rupa's ladder, the rung right after faith is long solitary study
the second rung is the company of devotees.
Narada never told the hunter to be gentle; the cruelty fell away by itself
he only said: break your bow, and chant. what didn't belong fell away, the way Rupa's ladder says it does.

games.q: after Narada's company and months of chanting by the river, the hunter brushes ants off his path. on Rupa's ladder, what is that?
o: the falling away of what doesn't belong: the cruelty simply went.
prema, the top rung, reached all at once.
nothing that counts; it's only good manners.
games.why: After faith, company and the work of devotion, what doesn't belong falls away. Nobody forced it; the heart was softening. Bhava and prema come further up.

practice: Think of one practice you'd like to keep coming back to: lighting the lamp, a bhajan, a few rounds of the name, a few quiet minutes. Name what usually gets in the way: the phone, the tiredness, the late night.
Then make one small plan for that moment, if this happens, then I'll do that. If you pray, offer the plan to Krishna. No rung is a grade; just notice honestly where you stand.

wordCard.voice: Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu: a book whose opening division climbs from a little faith, through company and practice, to prema, the heart made soft.

orig.note: Sanskrit prema, the fullest love; for Rupa, bhava grown dense, the heart made completely soft.

carryVoice: The line to keep: prema grows rung by rung, and the rung after faith is company. A hunter climbed it. Rupa's opening, complete.

sources.ref: Chaitanya Charitamrita, Madhya-lila 24 (Chaitanya tells Sanatana of Narada and the hunter Mrigari: the half-killed animals, the broken bow, chanting by the river, and the ants brushed from the path)
Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu 1.4.15–16 (the ladder: faith, company of the good, devotional work, removal of what is unwanted, steadiness, taste, attachment, bhava, prema)
Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu 1.3.1 (bhava like a ray of the sun of prema)
Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu 1.4.1 (prema: bhava made dense, the heart thoroughly softened, marked by intense sense of mine-ness)
